title: Some basic notes on the Nationals trading Curtis Mead for Connelly Early: ⚾️ Makes a lot of sense for a team that has an elite offense and poor pitching to trade a bat for an arm. WSH’s system, and especially their close-to-ready prospects, are also bat heavy. ⚾️ Connelly Early was one of Toboni’s guys in the BOS system. He drafted him in the 5th RD and the Sox developed him into a really nice arm. Great developmental win for the Sox. He added velo and sharpened his stuff. Toboni knows the player inside and out. ⚾️ In fact, he’s such a Toboni guy that I’ve been floating Early as a trade candidate for weeks (but in a Luis Garcia package with a prospect). Mead for Early is a surprising 1-for-1 because Mead was so lowly regarded as recently as April but clearly BOS is very high on his breakout being sustainable. ⚾️ Early is from Midlothian, Va. and went to UVA. He’s only 24 and he’s had lots of MLB success. For his career (21 starts and 111 innings) he’s posted a 3.24 ERA with 10 Ks per 9. ⚾️ Early throws a 4-seam FB (averages 94 MPH), 2-seam FB (92), a change-up 83), a curve ball (80), a slider (87), and a sweeper (82). He’s had the most success this season with his FB and SL. ⚾️ Early is currently on the IL. As long as his injury doesn’t end up getting worse and leading to a lengthy recovery, it’s mostly irrelevant to the deal. There is always risk with pitchers and especially pitchers on the shelf. ⚾️ While it’s very possible Early comes back healthy and pitches in the rotation this year, this trade is more about the future. This deal isn’t really about 2026. The Nats lack starting pitching talent at the MLB level and in the high minors. ⚾️ Early is under control for five more seasons after this year. He won’t be a FA until 2032 which is massive for WSH in building a rotation for the future. He and Cavalli will be mainstays. WSH just found a LHP to anchor 20% of their rotation for years to come. ⚾️ Mead is having a monster season. His play has been a major reason for WSH having the best offense in the sport. But if you’re WSH, how can you not flip him for a long term rotation-lock (and possible mid-rotation starter) months after acquiring him for a mid-level minor leaguer. ⚾️ Oh, and former first rounder Brady House has been hitting .300 in AAA and needs to play in the big leagues again. He will get run at 3B with Mead gone. The Nats also have RHH CIF Yohandy Morales waiting for a shot. He had been blocked at AAA, partially because of Mead. ⚾️ One more on Mead — he’s just 25 and he is under team control for 4 kore years. If this season is a real indicator of what he is, he will be a star in Boston. His game and swing are tailor made for Fenway Park. Overall I think giving up Mead is somewhat painful if this is who he’s going to be. That said he was a house money addition and the Nats kind of stumbled into his awesome season. They are potentially flipping him at PEAK value. I don’t think they could pass up a shot to land Early as pitching-starved as they are. And to have gotten Mead for what they did and traded him for Early? They flipped a house for crazy profit.
summary:
Some basic notes on the Nationals  trading Curtis Mead for Connelly Early:

⚾️ Makes a lot of sense for a team that has an elite offense and poor pitching to trade a bat for an arm. WSH’s system, and especially their close-to-ready prospects, are also bat heavy. 

⚾️ Connelly Early was one of Toboni’s guys in the BOS system. He drafted him in the 5th RD and the Sox developed him into a really nice arm. Great developmental win for the Sox. He added velo and sharpened his stuff. Toboni knows the player inside and out.

⚾️ In fact, he’s such a Toboni guy that I’ve been floating Early as a trade candidate for weeks (but in a Luis Garcia package with a prospect). Mead for Early is a surprising 1-for-1 because Mead was so lowly regarded as recently as April but clearly BOS is very high on his breakout being sustainable. 

⚾️ Early is from Midlothian, Va. and went to UVA. He’s only 24 and he’s had lots of MLB success. For his career (21 starts and 111 innings) he’s posted a 3.24 ERA with 10 Ks per 9. 

⚾️ Early throws a 4-seam FB (averages 94 MPH), 2-seam FB (92), a change-up 83), a curve ball (80), a slider (87), and a sweeper (82). He’s had the most success this season with his FB and SL.

⚾️ Early is currently on the IL. As long as his injury doesn’t end up getting worse and leading to a lengthy recovery, it’s mostly irrelevant to the deal. There is always risk with pitchers and especially pitchers on the shelf. 

⚾️ While it’s very possible Early comes back healthy and pitches in the rotation this year, this trade is more about the future. This deal isn’t really about 2026. The Nats lack starting pitching talent at the MLB level and in the high minors. 

⚾️ Early is under control for five more seasons after this year. He won’t be a FA until 2032 which is massive for WSH in building a rotation for the future. He and Cavalli will be mainstays. WSH just found a LHP to anchor 20% of their rotation for years to come.

⚾️ Mead is having a monster season. His play has been a major reason for WSH having the best offense in the sport. But if you’re WSH, how can you not flip him for a long term rotation-lock (and possible mid-rotation starter) months after acquiring him for a mid-level minor leaguer.

⚾️ Oh, and former first rounder Brady House has been hitting .300 in AAA and needs to play in the big leagues again. He will get run at 3B with Mead gone. The Nats also have RHH CIF Yohandy Morales waiting for a shot. He had been blocked at AAA, partially because of Mead. 

⚾️ One more on Mead — he’s just 25 and he is under team control for 4 kore years. If this season is a real indicator of what he is, he will be a star in Boston. His game and swing are tailor made for Fenway Park.

Overall I think giving up Mead is somewhat painful if this is who he’s going to be. That said he was a house money addition and the Nats kind of stumbled into his awesome season. They are potentially flipping him at PEAK value.

I don’t think they could pass up a shot to land Early as pitching-starved as they are. And to have gotten Mead for what they did and traded him for Early? They flipped a house for crazy profit.

⚾️ In fact, he’s such a Toboni guy that I’ve been floating Early as a trade candidate for weeks (but in a Luis Garcia package with a prospect). Mead for Early is a surprising 1-for-1 because Mead was so lowly regarded as recently as April but clearly BOS is very high on his breakout being sustainable.

⚾️ Oh, and former first rounder Brady House has been hitting .300 in AAA and needs to play in the big leagues again. He will get run at 3B with Mead gone. The Nats also have RHH CIF Yohandy Morales waiting for a shot. He had been blocked at AAA, partially because of Mead.

title: Rams HC Sean McVay spoke to 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan after his accident. “Most importantly, thank God he and the other person involved is okay,” McVay told reporters. “Perspective is everything. We talk about that all the time as coaches and everybody goes through different things. I think the most important thing is that he's on the road to recovery, his wife Mandy, and he's got a beautiful family, and I think any time that something like that happens, it shakes you up a little bit. But most importantly, I have talked to him. My thoughts and prayers are with him and his family, and I know he's got an incredible perspective on it all. Kyle's a stud. I have as much respect for him as anybody and he's a friend of mine, and I love him and hope that he's going to have a great recovery.”

title: Ella arrived at Newark Airport from Bellingham, Washington, in the middle of the night, January 2007. We were there waiting to welcome her, comfort her, and clean her off after a cross-country flight that changed her and our lives forever. She was a part of our family before we even became a family. Ella joined us before we married, before our son grew up, before our daughter was born, before we added four more dogs. She was a little chocolate brown labradoodle, who proved her strength and fierceness early on when she brought a dead baby bunny back into our house. She was, as my wife called her, my “constant companion.” Long before the pandemic and even after it, she quietly sat in my office, hearing every conversation, watching every live shot, knowing all the news before it was reported. She didn’t care what the stories were; she just was happy being with me. When she did leave my office, she loved walks and car rides. She always knew which button to push to lower the window so she could stick her head out and feel the wind in her face. Over the years, the rides and walks became more infrequent. She lost her vision and hearing. She developed doggy dementia, which led to seizures and breathing issues. She was in diapers. Her dark chocolate brown coat turned gray. But as much as her life changed, she was most happy in our arms or in our bed, laying with us, licking our faces. Yet Ella’s good days dwindled, and as tough as it was – and we agonized over it -- it became time to let her go. We did that Thursday, an all-time sad day. For the third time in just over 18 months, we lost one of our beloved furry friends, our other children. We lost Benny in January 2025, Bailey this March, and now Ella. It’s too much. We now are down to two dogs, Apple and Brady. Our house feels empty and our hearts feel broke. Ella’s pain has been transferred to us. Ella lived almost 20 years – she would have been 20 in November - and was a part of our graduations, celebrations, happy and sad moments. We know what we had and what she meant. But for all the time we had together -- and it was more than most get -- it still wasn’t enough. We always will remember and love our little Ellies.

title: NFL agent Sean Stellato has advanced to training camp with the Italian Men’s National Flag Football Team. Stellato will report to the Italian Olympic Committee Headquarters next month in Rome, where he will compete for a roster spot for the World Games in Germany. The top three teams at the World Games will qualify for the 2028 Olympic Games.
